identity: A single hadith of the classical Sunni collections (the Zayd b. Khalid al-Juhani report on luqata / found property and stray animals, Kitab al-Luqata). Classical prose, transmitted-report register. Two structural parts: an isnad (tokens 0-29, حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد ... عن زيد بن خالد الجهني) and a matn (30-92) which is a three-turn question-and-answer exchange with the Prophet: lost property, then the stray camel, then the stray sheep. 93 tokens, no <NL>, a single paragraph, so only the final token carries a mandatory stop.
law: The sentence unit here is the quotation-and-turn period, not the clause. Four rules follow. (1) The isnad is never broken: حدثنا X قال حدثنا Y ... عن Z is one chain, the transmission قال takes a colon and not a stop, and the chain runs on into the matn because عن زيد بن خالد الجهني أن النبي is grammatically bound, أن heading the complement of the عن chain. (2) A narrative frame verb plus فقال plus the quoted speech is ONE sentence, and it ends where the quoted speech ends, not at the فقال. (3) An interrogative closes a sentence, including the elliptical questioner turns فضالة الإبل and فضالة الغنم and the idiomatic وما لك ولها. (4) Everything coordinate inside one speech act is comma-level: the ثم ... ثم imperative chain, the فإن conditional, the hal clauses ترد الماء وترعى الشجر, and the ف of consequence in فذرها. Consequence of (2)+(4): stops fall only at turn changes and at interrogatives, giving one long opening period and then short alternating turns.
reasoning: Site 5 and site 9 (قال | حدثنا): rejected. These are transmission links inside the isnad, colon-level in every edition of this genre; breaking them would split a single chain of narration into fragments with no predicate. Site 29/30 (الجهني | أن): rejected, and this is the load-bearing one for the whole opening. أن النبي is not an independent assertion, it is the complement governed by عن زيد بن خالد الجهني, so a stop there severs a live grammatical dependency. That is why the first sentence legitimately runs 58 tokens. Site 39/40 (اللقطة | فقال): the most tempting false stop, since it is the hinge from narrative frame to the Prophet's speech. I reject it on the text's own internal evidence: the second فقال, at 69, cannot possibly be a sentence opening, because the sentence containing it demonstrably began at فغضب (61) with the parenthetical أو قال احمر وجهه sitting between them. The two فقال sites are structurally identical (frame verb, then ف of response, then quoted answer), so whatever I do at 69 I must do at 40. Both are clause-internal, and each answer's sentence therefore closes at the end of its quote, at 57 and at 72 respectively. Sites 43-46 (أو قال وعاءها وعفاصها) and 65-68 (أو قال احمر وجهه): rejected. These are the narrator's uncertainty parentheticals, set off by dashes in print. They interrupt a chain mid-flight (اعرف ... ثم عرفها; فغضب ... فقال) and can never be stops, and crucially the قال inside them is not a turn change but a hedge about wording. Sites 49 (سنة) and 52 (بها): rejected. اعرف ... ثم عرفها سنة ثم استمتع بها فإن جاء ربها فأدها إليه is one directive delivered as a ثم-chained sequence with a closing conditional; ثم here is enumerative within a single instruction, comma-level. Site 57 (إليه): STOP, hi. The directive completes at فأدها إليه, and the next token قال reopens the questioner's turn. Turn change is the hardest stop in a dialogic matn. Site 60 (الإبل): STOP, hi. قال فضالة الإبل is an elliptical interrogative turn, and what follows, فغضب, is narrative resumption. The ف there is no obstacle: this text itself shows ف opening a period. Site 72 (ولها): STOP, med, and my one genuinely contested site. وما لك ولها is interrogative in form though rhetorical in force, an idiom meaning what business have you with it. I take interrogative form as decisive since stops here are punctuation-derived, but I concede an editor could set it with a comma and run 70-83 as one period, which is why I do not claim hi. Sites 75, 77, 79: rejected. معها سقاؤها وحذاؤها is the justification, ترد الماء وترعى الشجر are hal clauses describing the camel, and فذرها حتى يلقاها ربها is the ف of consequence drawing the command out of that justification. One argumentative period, med confidence on holding 79 closed. Site 83 (ربها): STOP, hi. The second answer completes and قال at 84 is the questioner's third turn. Site 86 (الغنم): STOP, hi. Elliptical interrogative, exactly the shape already established at 60, and the answer follows at 87. Sites 88-91 (لك أو لأخيك أو للذئب): rejected, a three-way disjunction inside one verdict. Site 92 (للذئب): mandatory final stop. Net: six sentences, one long opening period carrying isnad plus first exchange, then five short dialogue turns.
